$$
p(x)=- 3 \cdot \sin{\left(x \right)},\quad q(x)=3 \cdot \cos{\left(x \right)},\quad n=2.
$$

- Equation III is a Bernoulli differential equation. In this case, we have

$$
p(x)=3,\quad q(x)=\sec{\left(x \right)},\quad n=-2.

Select all that apply."] [:db/add "e6954ca4-0576-566d-ba72-0d26e66452ab" :question/worked-solution "A Bernoulli differential equation has the form

$$
y'+p(x)y=q(x)y^n.
$$

- Equation I is *not* a Bernoulli differential equation. The normalized equation contains a function of $y$ that is not a single power of $y$.

- Equation II is a Bernoulli differential equation. In this case, we have

$$
p(x)=- e^{x},\quad q(x)=5 \cdot x^{2},\quad n=5.
$$

- Equation III is a Bernoulli differential equation. In this case, we have

$$
p(x)=2 \cdot \log{\left(x \right)},\quad q(x)=- 2 \cdot x,\quad n=3.
$$
